name: Question 12
problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y=-2{x}^{2}-4x+3
$$

has the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-2x}+Bx{e}^{-2x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.
worked_solution:
The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is a polynomial of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree $2,$ i.e.

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha {x}^{2}+\beta x+\gamma 
$$

where $\alpha ,$ $\beta ,$ and $\gamma $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=2\alpha x+\beta ,\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=2\alpha 
$$

To find the values of $\alpha ,$ $\beta $ and $\gamma ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
2\alpha +4(2\alpha x+\beta )+4(\alpha {x}^{2}+\beta x+\gamma )=-2{x}^{2}-4x+3
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives:

$$
4\alpha {x}^{2}+(8\alpha +4\beta )x+(2\alpha +4\beta +4\gamma )=-2{x}^{2}-4x+3
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}4\alpha =-2\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,{x}^{2}) \\ 8\alpha +4\beta =-4\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,x) \\ 2\alpha +4\beta +4\gamma =3\, & (\text{equating the constants})\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{1}{2},\beta =0,\gamma =1.$

Therefore, the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+1.
$$

Question 12
?

Given that the differential equation d2ydx2+4dydx+4y=−2x2−4x+3 has the complementary function yc(x)=Ae−2x+Bxe−2x, find the particular solution yp(x) to this equation.

a
 yp=2x2+2x−1
b
 yp=x2−x2+1
c
yp=−x22+1
d
 yp=−2x2+4x+1
e
 yp=x22−2x−12
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is a polynomial of degree 2. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree 2, i.e.

yp(x)=αx2+βx+γ where α, β, and γ are constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the first and second derivatives of yp gives:

dypdx=2αx+β,d2ypdx2=2α

To find the values of α, β and γ, we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

2α+4(2αx+β)+4(αx2+βx+γ)=−2x2−4x+3

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives:

4αx2+(8α+4β)x+(2α+4β+4γ)=−2x2−4x+3

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

{4α=−2(equating the coefficients ofx2)8α+4β=−4(equating the coefficients ofx)2α+4β+4γ=3(equating the constants)

Solving this system gives α=−12,β=0,γ=1.

Therefore, the particular integral yp(x) is

yp(x)=−x22+1.
